title: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: When starting a turbine engine
choices: a hot start is indicated if the exhaust gas temperature exceeds specified limits.
an excessively lean mixture is likely to cause a hot start.
release the starter switch as soon as indication of light-off occurs.
a hot start is indicated when the engine fails to light off.
questions.answerText: a hot start is indicated if the exhaust gas temperature exceeds specified limits.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A hot start occurs when exhaust-gas temperature exceeds the engine's permitted starting limit or rises too rapidly. Excess fuel or insufficient starter airflow can overheat turbine parts; follow the specific abort checklist.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What should be done initially if a turbine engine catches fire when starting?
choices: Continue starting attempt in order to blow out the fire.
Turn off the fuel and continue engine rotation with the starter.
Stop the starter immediately and close the intake to prevent further airflow.
Continue engine start rotation and discharge a fire extinguisher into the intake
questions.answerText: Turn off the fuel and continue engine rotation with the starter.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
For a turbine start fire, shut off fuel and continue starter rotation if directed by the aircraft procedure. Airflow can purge fuel and flame from the engine; use the approved fire checklist.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: A cool-off period prior to shutdown of a turbine engine is accomplished in order to
choices: increase compressor pressure before securing the engine.
prevent seizure of the engine bearings.
allow the turbine wheel to cool before the case contracts around it.
prevent vapor lock in the fuel control and/or fuel lines.
questions.answerText: allow the turbine wheel to cool before the case contracts around it.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A cool-off period lets turbine wheels and other hot-section parts cool gradually before shutdown. This reduces uneven thermal contraction, rubbing, and distortion; use the engine maker's stated time and conditions.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which of the following indicates that a combustion chamber of a jet engine is not operating properly?
choices: Warping of the exhaust duct liner.
An unusually high fuel quantity in the aircraft tanks.
Clam shells stick in thrust reverse position.
Hot spots on the tail cone.
questions.answerText: Hot spots on the tail cone.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A localized hot spot on the tail cone can indicate uneven combustor operation or abnormal hot-gas impingement. Compare exhaust patterns and inspect according to the engine troubleshooting procedure.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Fuel with high flash point
choices: Provides good ignition capabilities
Is safe for handling
Has low freezing point
Has high density
questions.answerText: Is safe for handling
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Flash point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid gives off enough vapor to ignite momentarily under a test method. A higher flash point generally reduces vapor ignition risk during handling, but does not make fuel nonflammable or remove other hazards.

**Engineering principle**
Flash point is not autoignition temperature or boiling point.

💡 **Memory hook:** Higher flash point = less easily ignited vapor at ordinary handling temperatures.

🎯 **Board tip:** Follow fuel safety procedures regardless of flash point.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What prevents fuel from vaporizing inside the tanks when the aircraft is at high altitude?
choices: Positive air pressure on the top surface of the fuel from the engine
Positive air pressure on the top surface of the fuel from ram air
Negative air pressure on the top surface of the fuel from the pneumatic system
Negative pressure on the top surface of the fuel from ram air
questions.answerText: Positive air pressure on the top surface of the fuel from ram air
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Maintaining a suitable positive pressure above fuel can suppress vapor formation by keeping tank pressure above the fuel’s vapor pressure under the operating condition. Aircraft tank venting and pressurization arrangements are installation-specific and must follow approved design data.

**Engineering principle**
Tank vent pressure control is different from the engine fuel pump’s delivery pressure.

💡 **Memory hook:** Higher tank pressure discourages boiling.

🎯 **Board tip:** Avoid treating a simplified exam answer as a universal description of every aircraft fuel tank.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which accessory is not found in an APU?
choices: Fuel pump
Oil pump
Electric generator
Hydraulic pump
questions.answerText: Hydraulic pump
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The accessory complement of an APU depends on its installation, but a hydraulic pump is not a standard accessory in the cited question. APUs commonly provide electrical power and bleed air; verify aircraft fit.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which component prevents cavitation at the inlet of the high pressure fuel pump?
choices: Fuel boost pumps in the tank
Low pressure fuel pump
LP fuel shut-off valve
Positive air pressure from ram air
questions.answerText: Low pressure fuel pump
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A low-pressure/boost pump supplies positive inlet pressure to the high-pressure pump. This reduces the risk of inlet starvation and cavitation, especially when fuel is hot, at altitude, or under high flow demand.

**Engineering principle**
The boost pump supports the high-pressure pump; the high-pressure pump supplies the metering unit at operating pressure.

💡 **Memory hook:** Feed the pump before asking it to raise pressure.

🎯 **Board tip:** Cavitation is an inlet-pressure problem, not simply a clogged nozzle.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which control lever is used on engines equipped with hydromechanical fuel control unit to open the fuel valves and starts the ignition?
choices: Forward thrust lever
Start lever
Reverse thrust lever
Master switch
questions.answerText: Start lever
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
On the referenced hydromechanical fuel control, the start lever initiates the start sequence and permits fuel introduction at the proper point. Exact lever logic is engine-specific.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What does the thrust reverser interlock system do?
choices: It prevents deployment of the reverser if the opposite reverser does not deploy
It prevents the engine from increasing power until the reverser is fully deployed
It prevents the reverser from deploying while in flight
It prevents the reverser from deploying when a fault is detected in the system
questions.answerText: It prevents the engine from increasing power until the reverser is fully deployed
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A thrust-reverser interlock prevents unsafe deployment or power increase while the reverser is in an incompatible position. It protects the engine and aircraft from unintended thrust and mechanical damage.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which statement is true with regards to heat exchangers?
choices: Air is used to cool the oil using a heat exchanger
Fuel heats up while the oil cools down in a heat exchanger
Oil heats up while the fuel cools down in a heat exchanger
Fuel and oil mixes inside a heat exchanger then separates when it leaves
questions.answerText: Fuel heats up while the oil cools down in a heat exchanger
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A fuel-oil heat exchanger transfers heat between fluids: warm oil may heat cold fuel, while fuel may cool hot oil. Which one gains heat depends on inlet temperatures and operating state.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which component experiences the highest heat-to- metal contact in a jet engine?
choices: Combustor
Ignition Plug
Fuel Nozzle
Turbine blades
questions.answerText: Turbine blades
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Turbine blades contact the hot gas after combustion while also carrying high centrifugal stress. Cooling passages, alloy, and coating protect them, but their temperature exposure makes inspection critical.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What happens when there is a leak in the fuel-oil heat exchanger?
choices: The fuel will contaminate the oil
The oil will contaminate the fuel
Both fuel and oil will be contaminated
No contamination since both fluid have the same pressure
questions.answerText: The fuel will contaminate the oil
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A leak through the heat-exchanger barrier can contaminate the lower-pressure fluid with the higher-pressure fluid. The keyed answer says fuel contaminates oil; actual direction depends on pressure differential, so inspect both circuits.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What happens to the lubrication system when the main filter gets clogged?
choices: Oil will stop flowing
Oil will continue to flow
Oil will flow thru the bypass valve
Oil will go in the reverse direction
questions.answerText: Oil will flow thru the bypass valve
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
When filter restriction creates excessive pressure drop, the bypass valve opens to preserve oil flow. Oil may then be unfiltered, but maintaining lubrication is safer than starving bearings; investigate the blockage.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Which statement is true with regards to oil viscosity?
choices: Oxidation does not affect viscosity
Oil pressure greatly affects viscosity
Oil viscosity decreases when oil temperature increases
Oil viscosity increases when oil temperature increases
questions.answerText: Oil viscosity decreases when oil temperature increases
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Oil viscosity generally decreases as temperature rises, so hot oil flows more readily and may provide a thinner lubricating film. Oil grade and pressure limits account for operating temperature.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What danger exist if thrust reversers are operated at low engine speed?
choices: Problems with directional stability
Possibility of ingesting its own exhaust
Ineffective braking
High EGT
questions.answerText: Possibility of ingesting its own exhaust
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
At low engine speed, exhaust may be ingested back toward the inlet during reverser operation, creating hot-gas reingestion or compressor disturbance. Follow the approved speed and ground-use limits.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What type of seal is used to seal the oil in a bearing sump?
choices: Magnetic carbon seals
Spring-loaded carbon seals
Labyrinth seals
O-ring
questions.answerText: Labyrinth seals
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Labyrinth seals use successive clearances and turns to restrict leakage without rubbing contact. This suits high-speed, hot rotating assemblies where contact seals can wear or overheat.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What would be the effect of an oil pressure relief valve getting stuck in the open position?
choices: High oil pressure will develop
Oil pressure will not develop sufficiently to lubricate
Oil will leak externally
Normal operation, oil will just return to the tank
questions.answerText: Oil pressure will not develop sufficiently to lubricate
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A relief valve stuck open continuously diverts oil, preventing pressure from reaching its required level. Low pressure threatens bearing lubrication and requires prompt action under the maintenance procedure.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: At what stage in a turbine engine is gas pressure the greatest?
choices: Turbine outlet
Compressor outlet
Compressor inlet
Exhaust Cone
questions.answerText: Compressor outlet
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Compressor stages progressively raise pressure, so the greatest gas pressure is normally at the compressor outlet before combustion. Pressure then falls as gas expands through turbine stages.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What is the primary function of an exhaust cone of a turbine engine?
choices: Align the exhaust gases to develop an efficient power
Straighten the swirling exhaust gasses.
Collect and convert exhaust gasses into a solid low-velocity exhaust vapor
Collect and convert exhaust gasses into a solid high-velocity exhaust jet
questions.answerText: Collect and convert exhaust gasses into a solid high-velocity exhaust jet
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The exhaust cone collects turbine discharge and shapes it into an organized high-velocity exhaust stream. It contributes to thrust by guiding flow, while a nozzle may provide further expansion depending on engine design.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: For what primary purpose is a turbine engine fuel control unit trimmed?
choices: Eliminate vibration in the compression section
To obtain maximum thrust output when desired
To properly position the power levers
To adjust the idle RPM
questions.answerText: To obtain maximum thrust output when desired
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Trimming calibrates the fuel-control schedule so the engine reaches specified maximum thrust while staying within temperature, speed, and pressure limits. It is a maintenance adjustment, not a routine cockpit control.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What is the primary role of the turbine-engine fuel control unit?
choices: Store all aircraft fuel
Control landing-gear extension
Meter fuel to meet commanded power while respecting engine operating limits
Set compressor blade geometry manually
questions.answerText: Meter fuel to meet commanded power while respecting engine operating limits
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The fuel control meters fuel to match commanded power while respecting engine limits such as turbine temperature and spool speed. Fuel flow therefore varies with operating conditions rather than being fixed.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What does an engine start lever commonly coordinate on a turbine engine?
choices: Cabin door locking
Fuel introduction and ignition/start sequencing
Propeller blade tracking
Oil analysis sampling
questions.answerText: Fuel introduction and ignition/start sequencing
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The start lever commonly coordinates fuel admission and ignition sequencing so fuel is introduced after adequate engine rotation and ignition availability. The specific sequence is defined by the engine checklist.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Why is turbine starting temperature monitored closely?
choices: Temperature controls wing loading
It measures fuel quantity
It sets starter current only
Excessive temperature during start can damage hot-section components
questions.answerText: Excessive temperature during start can damage hot-section components
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
During starting, engine airflow is limited while fuel is being introduced, making hot-section temperature rise quickly if combustion is excessive. Temperature monitoring helps prevent damage to combustor and turbine parts.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What is the purpose of a turbine-engine igniter during start?
choices: Remain continuously sparking at all normal conditions
Meter fuel to the burner
Control compressor speed
Provide an ignition spark until combustion becomes self-sustaining
questions.answerText: Provide an ignition spark until combustion becomes self-sustaining
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A turbine igniter supplies the spark that lights the fuel-air mixture during starting or a commanded relight. It normally stops firing after stable combustion is established.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What does an anti-ice system protect on a turbine-engine inlet?
choices: The starter relay from overload
Inlet surfaces where ice could restrict or disrupt airflow
The exhaust cone from corrosion only
The fuel-control gears from wear
questions.answerText: Inlet surfaces where ice could restrict or disrupt airflow
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Inlet anti-ice protects surfaces where ice could restrict airflow, distort compressor entry flow, or shed into the engine. The system may use hot bleed air or electrical heating depending on design.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Why is fuel recirculated through a fuel-oil heat exchanger on some engines?
choices: Increase fuel octane
Remove all fuel from the aircraft
Ignite the mixture before the combustor
Transfer heat between fuel and oil to manage their temperatures
questions.answerText: Transfer heat between fuel and oil to manage their temperatures
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Fuel recirculation lets a heat exchanger transfer energy between fuel and oil. It can warm cold fuel or cool hot oil depending on their relative temperatures, while the fluids remain separated.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: What does a fuel filter bypass arrangement protect against?
choices: Interruption of fuel flow if the filter becomes excessively restricted
Excessive propeller rpm
Oil foaming
A hot start
questions.answerText: Interruption of fuel flow if the filter becomes excessively restricted
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A filter bypass preserves fuel delivery if the element becomes excessively restricted, by routing fuel around it after a pressure threshold. This prevents fuel starvation but can allow contaminants downstream.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: Why are turbine-engine fuel nozzles checked for spray pattern?
choices: It changes the engine type
It controls oil pressure
Poor atomization or uneven distribution can create hot spots and unstable combustion
The pattern sets the fan bypass ratio
questions.answerText: Poor atomization or uneven distribution can create hot spots and unstable combustion
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A good nozzle spray atomizes and distributes fuel evenly for stable combustion. Poor pattern can create local hot spots, incomplete burning, or excessive turbine temperature.
tags: Gas Turbine Fuel, Control, Starting, Ignition, Lubrication, and Anti-Icing Systems

questions.question: In a dry-sump turbine-engine lubrication system, what is the purpose of the scavenge pump?
choices: Return oil from bearing sumps to the oil tank.
Meter fuel to the combustion chamber.
Increase compressor discharge pressure.
Supply hydraulic pressure to the propeller governor.
questions.answerText: Return oil from bearing sumps to the oil tank.
questions.explanation:
The scavenge pump removes oil from sumps and returns it to the tank; the pressure pump supplies lubricating oil to the engine.
